summary: Iraq has ended visa on arrival: visitors now need an e-Visa before they travel (USD 160 per the UK FCDO; Iraq's portal says it is valid 30 days, the FCDO says 60), or an embassy visa. The Kurdistan Region issues its own e-Visa, online or on arrival for many nationalities, valid only inside the Kurdistan Region.

notes: Australia's Smartraveller says it is illegal to photograph or film government buildings, checkpoints, military bases and embassies, and that you need approval to film in a public place.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says Iraq's economy is primarily cash-based, US dollars are accepted in some shops, and you may have difficulty finding an ATM that accepts an international card. Australia's Smartraveller says US dollars and euros are the easiest foreign currencies to exchange at banks and exchange bureaus.

safety.text: The FCDO advises against all travel to large parts of Iraq — including Kirkuk, Ninawa and Salah al-Din provinces, western Anbar and Sadr City — and against all but essential travel to the rest, including Baghdad and the Kurdistan Region. It reports Iranian strikes in Iraq, including the Kurdistan Region, since 8 July 2026. Terrorism, kidnapping and sudden unrest remain real risks; if you go, travel with an experienced local operator.

tips.text: The Kurdistan Region (Erbil, Sulaymaniyah) issues its own e-Visa, online or on arrival for many nationalities, but it is valid in the Kurdistan Region ONLY. Travelling from Erbil to Baghdad or Mosul requires a federal Iraqi e-Visa; decide which you need before you fly.

Canada's travel advice says Iraq's economy is primarily cash-based and ATMs that accept international cards are hard to find, so bring enough cash; Australia's Smartraveller says US dollars and euros are the easiest to exchange. The e-Visa itself is paid online when you apply.

The UK government says it is a legal requirement to carry photographic ID in Iraq and that the authorities stop people for ID checks at checkpoints within cities and on main roads. Always carry your passport and keep copies of your visa.

The UK government says the Arba'een pilgrimage attracts millions of pilgrims to Iraq and usually falls between August and September; Canada put the 2026 pilgrimage around 3 August and notes a heightened security risk. The UK advises following local dress codes.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Iraq?
faq.answer: Yes. Iraq no longer issues visit visas on arrival: the UK, Canadian and Australian governments all say you must get a visa before you travel, usually the e-Visa on Iraq's official portal (evisa.iq). The FCDO gives the fee as USD 160 and the validity as 60 days; Iraq's portal says 30 days, so plan on 30. Apply at least 24 hours before departure — airlines check for the visa before boarding. Nationalities not eligible for the e-Visa apply at an Iraqi embassy. Turkey's foreign ministry says Turkish citizens under 15 or over 50 are visa-exempt for 30 days. No official source we could read confirms whether Iranian citizens need a visa.

faq.question: Is a visa for the Kurdistan Region the same as an Iraqi visa?
faq.answer: No. The Kurdistan Regional Government issues its own e-Visa (visit.gov.krd), valid only inside the Kurdistan Region. Its portal says citizens of its 'Country List A' can get it online or on arrival at any KRI entry point, while others need a sponsor in the Region; the fee is IQD 100,000, the visa is valid 90 days from issue and allows a 30-day stay. To travel on to Baghdad or anywhere else in federal Iraq you need a separate Iraqi e-Visa.

faq.question: Is Iraq safe for tourists?
faq.answer: No. Canada and Australia advise against all travel to Iraq, and the UK advises against all travel to large parts of the country, including Kirkuk, Ninawa and Salah al-Din provinces, and against all but essential travel to much of the rest. Missile, drone and rocket attacks have struck locations in Iraq, including the Kurdistan Region. Check your government's advice before considering a trip.

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Iraq?
faq.answer: No. Israeli passport holders are not admitted to Iraq. Australia's Smartraveller says the authorities may also refuse entry if your passport contains Israeli stamps or visas.

faq.question: How do I apply and pay for the Iraqi e-Visa?
faq.answer: Online, on Iraq's e-Visa portal (evisa.iq), with a valid passport and a digital photo on a white background; the fee is paid by secure online payment and the visa arrives by email to print and show at the border. The FCDO gives the fee as USD 160. Apply at least 24 hours before you fly and carry a return or onward ticket, or the airline may refuse boarding.
